- **PRODUCT (P3, postgres-only): Stripe billing webhook re-sends a duplicate "Billing updated/attention" email on Stripe event RE-DELIVERY — the DATA reconcile is idempotent but the NOTIFICATION is not.**
  Found 2026-07-03T07:2xZ during a step-2(c) deeper money-side-effect 2nd-pass on the §8 Stripe webhook surface (the
  stalest high-risk ledger row, last swept 2026-07-02T19:50Z). The prior 19:50Z pass concluded "idempotency —
  reconcilers upsert … so Stripe retries/replays are safe," which is true for the DB writes but conflated
  data-idempotency with notification-idempotency. `handleStripeBillingEvent` (`lib/server/stripe-billing.ts:127`) runs
  `reconcile → recordAudit → notify` with **NO pre-check of whether `event.id` was already processed** (scripted grep:
  no `already`/`existing`/`select … admin_audit_entries` guard in the file). Because Stripe delivers webhooks
  **at-least-once** and retries any non-2xx, the SAME `event.id` can arrive twice; the reconcilers are safe (UPSERT on
  deterministic keys `sub-${providerSubscriptionId}` / `inv-${providerInvoiceId}` / audit `stripe-event-${event.id}`
  with `on conflict do update`), but `notifyStripeBillingChange` fires on **every** `result.reconciled===true`
  (`stripe-billing.ts:247`) and `notifyBillingChanged` (`lib/server/notifications.ts:344`) calls `sendNotification`
  **unconditionally** — no idempotency gate. So a redelivered `invoice.paid`/`checkout.session.completed` sends the
  company's billing contact a **duplicate** email. Same defect CLASS as the gemmatch/completion duplicate-email that was
  explicitly guarded (`wasAlreadyCompleted` pre-update check) — here there's no equivalent. **NOT force-fixed
  autonomously:** this is a money/billing + notification-firing path and postgres-only (the `admin_audit_entries` dedup
  source is postgres), with NO live DB to verify this run; the correct fix (gate `notify` on first-sighting of
  `event.id` — e.g. detect a fresh audit insert via `returning (xmax = 0) as inserted`, or SELECT the audit row before
  reconcile) reorders/adds a query in a money path and needs live webhook-replay + DB verification. Flagged PRODUCT for
  human triage per the money/hire + notification-rule caution. No live-exposure severity beyond a duplicate email
  (no double-charge — checkout is a hosted payment link, reconcile is idempotent). No code change this run. tsc exit 0;
  qa:notifications 0/0; all imports resolve.

- **[RESOLVED — see Done 2026-07-03T01:4xZ] P1 (was BLOCKED): Interview RSVP endpoint has NO authorization — cross-tenant write / arbitrary interview cancellation.** Codex landed `requireRecipientOrStoreAccess` on this route; cross-tenant write hole closed fail-closed. Static+tsc verified sound this run.
  `app/api/interviews/[id]/rsvp/route.ts` POST takes only the URL `id` + `response` and calls
  `updatePostgresInterviewRsvp({ interviewId, response })` (postgres) or `updateInterviewRsvp(id, response)`
  (local) directly — **neither the route nor either mutation performs any `requireStoreAccess`, ownership, or
  tenant check.** Both mutations resolve the interview by id alone (`update interviews … where id = $4`
  wrapped by `updatePostgresInterviewRsvp`; local `store.interviews.find(id)`), so any authenticated session
  (middleware only checks a session cookie exists — no tenant binding) can POST to
  `/api/interviews/<any-interview-id>/rsvp` and mutate an interview belonging to **any other store/tenant**.
  Severity is elevated because `response:"declined"` sets `status:"cancelled"` in BOTH runtimes
  (`lib/local-api-store.ts:1310`; postgres RSVP path mirrors it) — so this is not a benign RSVP flag but an
  **arbitrary cross-tenant interview-cancellation** primitive. Prior interview sweeps verified the store-scoped
  GET and the `interviews/[id]` PATCH/DELETE (both resolve `getPostgresInterviewStoreId` → `requireStoreAccess`
  first), but this separate applicant-facing RSVP route was never guarded.
  Recommended fix (needs applicant-flow **browser verify (human)** before landing, since it's coupled to the
  fragile applicant-identity model — see the Maya-only seed limitation): the route should resolve the
  interview's application recipient email and require `getSessionContext().email` to match it
  (case-insensitive), i.e. only the candidate who owns the interview may RSVP; admins/store users could be
  allowed via `canAccessStore(interview.storeId)` as a secondary branch. This needs a new resolver returning the
  interview's recipient email (only `getPostgresInterviewStoreId` exists today) + parity in the local store, and
  the email-match must be verified against how applicant sessions actually carry email in the running app —
  hence flagged for human decision rather than force-changed in an unverifiable autonomous run. Not a
  one-token fix; do NOT swap in a bare `requireStoreAccess(storeId)` — applicants are not store users, so that
  would break the legitimate RSVP flow.

  Found 2026-07-02T01:0xZ during a fresh sweep of the applicant-facing write routes (the stale `lib/*`/applicant
  surface, step 2(b), since Open held only BLOCKED + PRODUCT items). `app/api/gemmatch/responses/route.ts` POST
  validates ONLY that `body.inviteId` is present, then completes the GemMatch response keyed by that invite id alone:
  `completePostgresGemMatchResponse({ inviteId, pickedAdjectiveIds })` (postgres) or

  `requireStoreAccess`, ownership, or session-identity check** — both resolve the invite by bare id
  (`postgres-phase1.ts:3211 completePostgresGemMatchResponse` updates `where id = $1`; local
  `lib/local-api-store.ts:809` does `store.gemmatchInvites.find(id)`), and middleware only checks that *a* session
  cookie exists (no tenant binding). So any authenticated session can POST `/api/gemmatch/responses` with **any
  other tenant's** `inviteId` and (a) overwrite that candidate's picked-adjective set / computed GemMatch result and
  (b) trigger `notifyCompletion` → `notifyAssessmentCompleted` emails to that tenant's candidate AND manager
  (`getPostgresGemMatchCompletionNotificationContext`). Same defect CLASS as the interview-RSVP item above:
  applicant-facing write, no identity binding, elevated by a real email/data side-effect.
  **NOT force-fixed** (same reason the RSVP item is BLOCKED): the correct fix is coupled to the fragile
  applicant-identity model — applicants are NOT store users, so a bare `requireStoreAccess(invite.storeId)` would
  break the legitimate candidate completion flow. Recommended fix (needs **browser verify (human)** of how applicant
  sessions carry email in the running app): resolve the invite → its application recipient email and require
  `getSessionContext().email` to match (case-insensitive); allow store users/admins via `canAccessStore(invite.storeId)`
  as a secondary branch. Needs a new resolver returning the invite's recipient email + local-store parity (only
  `getPostgresGemMatchCompletionNotificationContext` exists today, and it's used post-completion for notification, not
  as a pre-auth gate). Live click-through not available this run → do NOT swap in a bare guard autonomously.

- **[RESOLVED — see Done 2026-07-03T04:12Z] PRODUCT: Postgres job-detail resolver ignores tenant → wrong job / spurious 404 on cross-tenant slug collision (P2, postgres-only).**
  Found 2026-07-02T15:0xZ during a deeper 2nd-pass on multi-tenant data scoping (step 2(c): Open held only
  BLOCKED+PRODUCT and the whole Coverage ledger was <24h swept), triggered by Codex's 13:20 rebuild of
  `app/api/stores/[storeId]/jobs/[slug]/route.ts` (was 501-stubbed, now live — see item above). The route resolves the
  job via `getPostgresJobDetail(params.slug)` → `resolvePostgresJobBySlug(slug)` (`postgres-phase1.ts:2326`), which
  queries `public_jobs` by `id/slug/title` match GLOBALLY (no `store_id` predicate), `order by status(open<draft<
  paused<closed), opened_at desc, created_at desc limit 1`. Because `public_jobs` has `unique (store_id, slug)` (NOT a
  global unique — migration `0001_phase1_core.sql:246`), two tenants CAN own the same slug (e.g. `bench-jeweler`). When
  they collide, the resolver returns whichever ranks first by that ORDER BY (e.g. the `open` one), not the caller's.
  Security is fine — fail-closed: the route's post-check `detail.job.storeId !== storeId → 404` blocks any cross-tenant
  read/write. The DEFECT is functional/availability: a store owner requesting their OWN job (e.g. a `paused`
  `bench-jeweler`) can get a spurious **"Job not found" 404** when another tenant's same-slug job outranks it. Same
  un-scoped-resolve pattern also feeds `updatePostgresStoreJob` (via `resolvePostgresJobBySlug(input.jobId)`,
  `:2256`) and the top-level `app/api/jobs/[slug]/{route,pause,close,open,applicants}` routes (all call
  `getPostgresJobDetail`). Postgres-only — the active in-memory runtime uses `getLocalStoreJob(storeId, slug)` which IS
  store-scoped, so today's live path is unaffected; and collision needs two tenants to pick the same slug (unlikely in
  current seed). The correct fix — thread `storeId` into `getPostgresJobDetail`/`resolvePostgresJobBySlug` (an OPTIONAL
  param keeps the ~8 existing callers compiling) and add `and store_id = $N` to the WHERE — is a shared-signature +
  schema-aware SQL change across the 283KB postgres file with NO live DB to verify this run, so it's broader than one
  safe atomic static change. Flagged for product/human triage, NOT force-changed. tsc exit 0; no code change this run.
  **UPDATE 2026-07-03T04:12Z — current code has this fix.** `resolvePostgresJobBySlug(slug, storeId?)` now adds
  `and store_id = $3` when a store id is provided; `getPostgresJobDetail(slug, storeId?)` threads that optional
  scope; and `app/api/stores/[storeId]/jobs/[slug]/route.ts` passes the authorized store id on GET/PATCH. The
  store-scoped route can no longer resolve the wrong tenant's same-slug job before its post-check. Top-level
  diagnostic `/api/jobs/[slug]/*` routes intentionally remain global but mutate by resolved job store after
  `requireStoreAccess(current.job.storeId, "jobs.update")`.

- **[RESOLVED — see Done 2026-07-03T04:12Z] PRODUCT: Applicant training progress can't persist in the postgres runtime (P2).**
  `app/(associate)/portal/training/page.tsx:36` posts to `POST /api/course-assignments/[id]/progress` when an
  applicant clicks Start/Continue. In the in-memory runtime this works (no store gate; `updateTrainingProgress`
  persists progress + pushes the resume credential). But the postgres branch of that route calls
  `requireStoreAccess(storeId, "course_assignments.progress")` — an applicant is not a store user, so
  `canAccessStore` denies it and the POST 403s. The page's `.catch(() => undefined)` swallows the error, so the
  optimistic progress bar/status update is local-only and is lost on the next reload/fetch. Same
  optimistic-non-persistence class as the Training Center player and profile prefs, but here rooted in an
  auth-model gap: there's no applicant-scoped progress path in postgres. Options: (a) add an applicant-owned
  progress endpoint/branch that authorizes by the assignment's `recipientEmail` instead of store membership, or
  (b) gate the button to store users only. Postgres-only (in-memory Phase-1 works today); broader than one
  atomic item, so flagged for product, not changed.
  **UPDATE 2026-07-03T04:12Z — current code has this fix and live proof.** The route now resolves the assignment
  first, then calls `requireRecipientOrStoreAccess({ storeId: before.storeId, recipientEmail: before.recipientEmail,
  operation: "course_assignments.progress" })` before `updatePostgresTrainingProgress`, so applicants can update
  their own assignment while cross-recipient writes remain fail-closed. Live smoke created a temporary non-completion
  assignment for Maya, confirmed it appeared in `/api/applicant/training`, posted progress 10%, confirmed refetch
  persistence as `In progress`, and deleted the temp assignment. Report:
  `docs/qa-runs/applicant-training-progress-2026-07-03T04-12-10-281Z/report.md`.

- **PRODUCT (P2, postgres-only): Store Pipeline silently caps at 25 applicants in the postgres runtime — no pagination/load-more UI, so a store with >25 candidates loses the overflow.**
  Found 2026-07-05T22:3xZ during a fresh step-2(b) re-sweep of the `pipeline` surface (stalest ledger cluster, last touched 2026-07-03 >24h; Open held only PRODUCT/RESOLVED/CLOSED/BLOCKED). `app/(store)/pipeline/page.tsx:119` fetches `/api/store/applications` with **no `?limit=`** param. The route (`app/api/store/applications/route.ts`) never sets a limit either, so it flows straight into `listPostgresApplicationSummaries({storeId,query,stage})`. But `listPostgresApplicationSummariesWithClient` (`lib/server/postgres-phase1.ts:4948`) defaults `limit = Math.min(Math.max(input.limit ?? 25, 1), 100)` → **25**, and the SQL ends `order by a.last_activity_at desc limit $4`. So the postgres runtime returns at most 25 rows while `total` (`count(*) over()`) still reflects the true count — the page's "{rows.length} of {apiRows.length}" (`page.tsx:179`) header would show e.g. "25 of 60", and there is NO next-page / load-more control anywhere on the page to reach applicants 26+. The active in-memory runtime is unaffected: the local branch (`getApplicantStore().listStoreApplicationSummaries` → `listStoreApplications` → `listApplications(storeId, query, stage)`, `lib/server/stores/applicant-store.ts:205`) applies **no limit** and returns every matching application, so this is a local-vs-postgres parity gap, not a live-runtime break. Everything else on the pipeline traced sound this run (route tenant-guarded via `requireStoreAccess(storeId,"applications.list")` + `withApiErrorHandling` in both runtimes; item shape matches `ApiApplicationItem` field-for-field in both `summarizeApplication` and `mapApplicationSummary`; `FitTier`=exactly the 4 Fit-filter options; JewelCert filter=only the 3 reachable statuses; all 6 `Icon*` exported; both empty states + `.catch`→PIPELINE seed fallback present; all row-action links resolve). **NOT force-fixed** — the correct fix is a UX/product decision (add cursor/offset pagination + a "Load more"/pager control, or at minimum thread `limit:100` from the route and surface a "showing first N" notice) that changes a shared query surface and the page layout, broader than one atomic surgical change and with no live DB to verify pagination this run. Flagged PRODUCT for human triage. No code change this run. Source-only `tsc` clean; no defect in the active runtime.

- **2026-07-03T02:2xZ — FIXED (real defect, P1 open-redirect): `auth/google/callback` `safeNext` accepted a backslash bypass → external open redirect after OAuth login.** Step 2(b): Open held only BLOCKED/PRODUCT/evidence items; picked the stalest ledger area (`auth/session routes`, dated 07-01, >24h) — re-sweep prompted by Codex's <2h `app/api/auth/logout/route.ts` re-edit (which itself re-verified SOUND: all cookie setters use `path:"/"`, matching `cookies.delete`'s default path, so SESSION/OAUTH_STATE/OAUTH_NEXT all clear; fixed `/login` redirect, no open-redirect; GET→POST idempotent). The real defect was in the sibling `safeNext` guard shared by the session routes: `value.startsWith("/") && !value.startsWith("//")` is NOT sufficient — a value like `/\evil.com` (or `/\/evil.com`) starts with `/`, its 2nd char is `\` (not `/`) so it passes, but `new URL("/\\evil.com", base)` is normalized by the WHATWG parser (backslash→slash for http/https) to `https://evil.com/`, an EXTERNAL host. Verified reachable in the production OAuth flow: `auth/google/start` stores `next` checking only `startsWith("/")` (accepts `/\evil.com`) into `OAUTH_NEXT_COOKIE`, and `auth/google/callback` passes it through `safeNext`→`new URL(...)` as the post-login redirect. So a crafted `/api/auth/google/start?next=/\evil.com` phishing link redirects a freshly-authenticated victim to an attacker host. Every prior auth sweep (passes 11–17) called this guard "open-redirect guarded" but none tested the backslash bypass. **Fix (surgical, 1 file):** hardened `safeNext` in `app/api/auth/google/callback/route.ts` to also reject `value.includes("\\")` (node-verified: `/\evil.com`, `/\/evil.com`, `//evil.com`, `https://evil.com` all → `/`; `/dashboard`, `/portal?x=1`, `/admin` preserved). **Verify:** braces/parens/brackets balanced (23/23, 66/66, 4/4), `@/lib/server/auth` import resolves, `npm exec tsc --noEmit` **exit 0**. qa:auth env-blocked only (`spawnSync gcloud ENOENT` — not installed in sandbox; unrelated to this code change). - [x] **2026-07-02T18:21Z · FIXED a notification firing-rule defect: `sendNotification`'s Postmark `fetch` could reject and 500 an already-committed write (P2, whole-class).** Step-2(c): no source changed since the 18:16Z run (newest mtime still the 17:32 hire route, `git HEAD e3678f5` unchanged) so there were no new Codex edits to regress-check → did a deeper 2nd-pass on the highest-risk notification-firing surface (Codex touched `postgres-phase1.ts`, which houses the notify-context resolvers, at 17:00). **Defect:** every notification is a *post-commit* side-effect — callers create the invite / complete the GemMatch / confirm the hire / submit the application / change billing, then `await notify…`. `sendNotification` (`lib/server/notifications.ts`) guards recipient/disabled/dryRun/token and maps a non-ok HTTP response to `{status:"failed"}`, but the `await fetch(...)` itself was **not** wrapped — so a transient network rejection (Postmark unreachable) would propagate as an unhandled rejection → `withApiErrorHandling` → **500 on an already-committed write**. On the client that reads as "action failed"; on retry the idempotency guards suppress the email, and non-idempotent creators (JewelCert invite) would duplicate. The hire route's author already documented this exact hazard and worked around it per-caller with `.catch(() => undefined)`, but every OTHER call site (`jewelcert-invites`, `gemmatch/responses`→`notifyCompletion`, `public/stores/[slug]/applications` candidate+manager, `stores/[storeId]/users`, `admin/companies/[id]/users`, `admin/users/[id]/resend`, `stripe-billing`) does a bare un-caught `await notify…`. **FIX (single file, additive/surgical):** wrapped the `fetch` in `sendNotification` in try/catch, returning `{status:"failed", provider:"postmark", reason:"postmark_network_error"}` on rejection — consistent with the existing non-ok-HTTP branch and the `"failed"` status already in the `NotificationResult` union; centralizes the guard so every caller is covered without touching any route. No behavior change when notifications are disabled/dryRun (still early-returns). Left the hire route's per-caller `.catch()` in place (harmless defense-in-depth). **Verify:** braces balanced ({}150/150, ()125/125, []14/14); `NotificationResult.status` union includes `"failed"`; `npm exec tsc -- --noEmit` **exit 0** (whole tree); `npm run qa:notifications` **0 blockers / 0 warnings, send adapter found**.   length-guarded `timingSafeEqual` (constant-time); `loginWithPassword` normalizes email, joins active

  bad-password (no user enumeration); DB-missing → `config`. **`firebase-auth`:** `verifyFirebaseIdToken` is a
  full RS256 JWT verification — enforces `alg=RS256`+`kid`, fetches Google's public certs (cached per
  `cache-control max-age`, ≥60s, −30s skew), verifies the RSA-SHA256 signature over `header.payload`, then
  validates `aud===projectId`, `iss===securetoken.google.com/<projectId>`, `sub`, `exp>now`, `iat<=now+60`, and
  `email_verified!==false`. **`storage-runtime`:** `getStorageRuntime` defaults to `local` unless
  `JEWELHIRE_STORAGE=postgres` AND a DB URL is set (safe fallback); `selectStoreAdapter` throws
  `StorageAdapterUnavailableError` when a postgres adapter is absent. **`api-errors` (high-value cross-check):**
  `withApiErrorHandling` catches and maps `UnauthenticatedError`→401, `AccessDeniedError`→**403**,
  `StorageAdapterUnavailableError`→501, else 500 — this **retroactively validates the 23-route

  scores correctly via `scoreGemMatch(resolveGemMatchPickedTexts(...))`). **Fix (additive/surgical, one
  file):** imported `ADJECTIVES` + `score as scoreGemMatch` from `@/lib/gemmatch`; resolve each submitted
  pick (slugified ID *or* raw text — mirrors the postgres resolver, reusing the file's existing `slugify`)
  back to canonical adjective text, then `primary = pickedTexts.length ? scoreGemMatch(pickedTexts).primary :
  "F"` (Foundation fallback only for empty/legacy submissions, preserving prior default). Removed the now-
  unused `profileCodes` local. Verified: no leftover `profileCodes` refs; parens/braces/brackets balanced
